name: search_monster
description: Find monster statblocks in the Cairn bestiary by words in their name, id, or description. Every word in the query must appear. Each result gives the statblock's stats, armor, and attacks, which create_monster can use as a template.

query.description: Words to look for, such as 'wolf' or 'giant spider'.

name: create_monster
description: Create a monster NPC in the world. Give a template to start from a bestiary statblock (see search_monster), and any value you give replaces the template's. Without a template, give a description and every stat: hit_points, strength, dexterity, and willpower are required. Attacks replace the template's attacks when given.

name.description: The monster's name, such as 'Grey Wolf'. It must be new.

location.description: The name of the location it is at.

description.description: What the monster looks like and how it behaves. Required without a template.

template.description: The id of a bestiary statblock to start from, as listed by search_monster.

hit_points.description: Hit Protection, the first damage it takes.

strength.description: Strength, which takes damage that gets past Hit Protection.

dexterity.description: Dexterity, used for initiative in the first round.

armor.description: Armor, subtracted from each hit before it reaches Hit Protection. Leave it out to use the template's, or 0 without one.

attacks.description: The monster's attacks, each with a name and dice such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'. Replaces the template's attacks when given.

name.description: The attack's name, such as 'bite'.

dice.description: The damage dice, such as '1d8' or '1d6+1d6'.

name: attack
description: Make an NPC's attack against a character. Attacks always hit. The attack's damage is rolled by the engine and reduces the target's armor, then Hit Protection, then Strength, and a target whose Strength is used up must make a Strength save. Use it only when the attacker's side is acting, after the initiative is set. Player characters attack with player_attack, not this tool. A detachment (a statblock marked as a group) is hit only by impaired attacks. A detachment's own attack has Blast: the engine rolls its enhanced damage separately for each living individual on the other side, and the target you name is one of them. A detachment whose Strength is used up makes a Strength save; if it fails it is broken, and the attack and targeting are refused until resolve_detachment is called.

attacker.description: The name of the NPC attacking.

attack.description: The name of one of the attacker's attacks, as the statblock lists it.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

modifier.description: The attack's modifier. 'normal' is the attack's own dice; 'impaired' and 'enhanced' roll different dice. Leave it out for a normal attack.

name: player_attack
description: Record the player character's attack against a target. Attacks always hit, so the player only rolls the damage. Use it when the player says what they attack with and the target is in the encounter. The target takes the damage through its armor, Hit Protection, and Strength, as with an NPC attack. A detachment can only be hit by an impaired attack.

target.description: The name of the character or NPC being attacked.

weapon.description: The weapon or means of attack, such as 'longsword'.

damage_dice.description: The damage dice for this attack, such as '1d8' for a longsword or '1d6+1d6' for two dice. Use the weapon's dice from the player character's statblock.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Roll your longsword damage.'

modifier.description: The attack's modifier. 'normal' is the attack's own dice; 'impaired' and 'enhanced' roll different dice. Leave it out for a normal attack.

name: player_save
description: Ask the player character to make the save they owe after their Strength was used up. The player rolls a d20 and the engine decides whether it passed. Use it when the player character's statblock shows a save due.

player_input.details: Save: roll 1d20 and succeed on a roll at or under your score.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Make your Strength save.'

name: player_initiative
description: Ask the player character to make their DEX save for initiative in the first round of an encounter. Call it once for each player character the encounter says is waiting for initiative. The result says whether more are still waiting, and when none are, the turn order is set and the first turn begins.

player_input.details: Initiative: roll 1d20 and pass on a roll at or under your Dexterity.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Make your Dexterity save for initiative.'

name: set_armor
description: Set a character's armor, which is subtracted from each hit before it reaches Hit Protection. Use it when a character puts on or takes off armor, or when a monster's armor changes.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

armor.description: The new armor value, from 0 (none) to 3 (heaviest armor).

name: recover_character
description: Bring a player character back from critical damage, where they were left unconscious and bleeding out. Use it only for a player character whose statblock shows Status: in critical damage. Narrate how they survived, such as being dragged to safety, bandaged in time, or kept alive by a companion, and what it cost them, such as a lasting injury, a lost possession, or a debt. The harm they took stays as it was.

name.description: The name of the player character.

explanation.description: How they survived, in a sentence or two.

consequence.description: What it cost them, in a sentence or two.

name: resolve_attacks
description: Resolve several NPC attacks on one character at once, such as two foes attacking the same character or one NPC using two weapons. Each attack rolls its own dice, only the single highest roll hits, and the damage is applied once. Every attacker must be a living NPC on the side opposing the target, and the whole list is checked before any dice are rolled. Use it only when the attackers' side is acting, after the initiative is set. Player characters attack with player_attack, not this tool.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

attacks.description: The attacks to resolve, one entry per attack.

attacker.description: The name of the NPC attacking.

attack.description: The name of one of the attacker's attacks, as the statblock lists it.

modifier.description: The attack's modifier. 'normal' is the attack's own dice; 'impaired' and 'enhanced' roll different dice. Leave it out for a normal attack.

name: harm_character
description: Harm a player character outside combat, from a fall, poison, exposure, or a similar hazard. Only the outside-harm stats can take it. Narrate what hurt them. Harm that takes their STR to 0 defeats them. Use it only for harm that does not come from a combat attack.

name.description: The name of the player character.

stat.description: The stat that takes the harm.

amount.description: How much harm to take, from the hazard's roll.

cause.description: What did the harm, in a few words.

name: end_condition
description: End a condition a player character has, when its ending happens in the story, such as a rest, first aid, the time running out, or a decision of yours. Use the trigger the condition names, or gm to end it by your decision.

name.description: The name of the player character.

condition.description: The id of the condition to end, such as walloped or broken_limb.

name: retreat
description: Have a non-player character try to run from the encounter. The engine makes its DEX save. Pass safe as true only when the NPC has a safe way out; if not, the attempt is refused. A passed save takes the NPC out of the fight. A failed save leaves it in the fight.

name.description: The name of the NPC running.

safe.description: True when the NPC has a safe destination to run to.

name: surrender
description: Have a character give up the fight and lay down arms. A surrendered character takes no more part in the encounter. The encounter ends once one side has nobody left who can fight.

name.description: The name of the character surrendering.

name: resolve_detachment
description: Decide what happens to a detachment whose Critical Damage save failed. 'defeat' breaks it and defeats it. 'flee' breaks it up and its members run from the fight. Until this is called, a broken detachment cannot attack or be attacked. Call it only after a detachment's Strength save has failed.

name.description: The name of the broken detachment.

outcome.description: 'defeat' if the detachment is broken and defeated, 'flee' if it breaks up and runs.

name: roll_tables
description: Roll on one or more of the Warden's dice tables and log every result. Use 'reaction' (2d6) for how an NPC or monster reacts to the party. Use 'die_of_fate' (1d6) when the outcome of an event is uncertain: 4 or more favors the PCs, 3 or less is bad luck. To create a monster, roll all eight monster_ tables (one 1d20 each) in a single call, then combine the results into a statblock and place it with create_monster. The engine does not save or place a creature from these rolls; you receive the results and decide what they mean.

tables.description: The ids of the tables to roll on, in order. Each is rolled once.

name: player_retreat
description: Ask the player character to make their DEX save to run from the encounter. Pass safe as true only when there is a safe destination to run to; if not, the attempt is refused. A passed save takes the character out of the fight. A failed save leaves them in it.

player_input.details: Run: roll 1d20 and get clear on a roll at or under your Dexterity.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to do, such as 'Make your Dexterity save to run.'

safe.description: True when there is a safe destination to run to.

name: advance_time
description: Move the campaign clock forward. Use it when time passes in the fiction: days, or parts of a day (morning, afternoon, evening, night). The result says when a new day begins and lists places not visited for a while, so update anything that should change.

days.description: Whole days to advance, from 0 to 365. Defaults to 0.

parts.description: Parts of a day to advance, from 0 to 12. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

name: rest
description: Record a rest for the whole party. The Warden decides the length from what the party does: 'moments' is a short break such as a drink and a sit-down, 'night' is a full night until morning, 'week' is a week of rest. The rest moves the clock forward itself, so do not also advance_time for the same time. Set interrupted when something breaks the rest, and then it counts as moments only. A full rest, uninterrupted, is the only way to clear Fatigue. A deprived character recovers nothing. Rest eats one ration per character itself (a lodged character uses the bed instead), so never remove rations before resting; a character with no ration is deprived.

length.description: How long the rest lasts: 'moments', 'night', or 'week'.

interrupted.description: True when something breaks the rest. An interrupted rest counts as moments only. Defaults to false.

reason.description: What the party was doing, such as 'camped in the ruined chapel'.

name: rest_history
description: Look up the party's recent rests and each character's last full rest, to decide whether a character is deprived.

name: set_deprivation
description: Mark a character as deprived of a crucial need, such as food or rest, or clear it. Call it as soon as the need goes unmet, before advancing time, so the engine can count the days. A deprived character recovers nothing, and the engine adds one Fatigue for each new day past the first. Check rest_history first when the cause is rest.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

deprived.description: True to mark the character as deprived, false to clear it.

cause.description: What the character is deprived of, such as 'no food for two days' or 'no full night's rest since the flood'.

name: add_fatigue
description: Add one Fatigue to a character's inventory because of something in the fiction, such as casting a spell or a shock. Fatigue takes one slot and lasts until a full night's rest. A deprived character is refused unless force is true: the engine adds deprivation Fatigue each day.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

cause.description: What caused the Fatigue, such as 'cast a spell'.

force.description: True only for a deprived character when something besides the deprivation causes this Fatigue.

name: give_spellbook
description: Give a character a spellbook holding one spell. It takes one slot. Casting from it costs one Fatigue.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

description.description: The spell's text, as the Warden writes it.

name: give_scroll
description: Give a character a scroll holding one spell. Scrolls are petty and take no slot. One cast spends the scroll and costs no Fatigue.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

description.description: The spell's text, as the Warden writes it.

name: give_relic
description: Give a character a relic with a number of uses. `recharge` is the rule for restoring its uses, written as text. A relic adds no Fatigue.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

uses.description: How many uses the relic has when full.

recharge.description: The rule that restores its uses, such as 'Capture the final breath of a dying warrior.'

name: cast_spell
description: Cast a spell the character says they cast. From a spellbook it costs one Fatigue. From a scroll the scroll is spent and no Fatigue is added. Use it for every cast so the cost is recorded.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

name: use_relic
description: Spend one use of a relic. It fails when the relic has no uses left, until it recharges.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

name: use_item
description: Spend one use of a consumable the character carries, such as a torch, oil, bandages, or a salve. The last use uses it up and removes it. Call this only when the character deliberately uses up that exact item (pouring the oil, applying the bandage). Never spend it for an action that uses a different item, for an attempt that fails, or for holding something in a flame that is already burning: a lit lantern or torch burns down over time, not per action. Not for relics (use use_relic), spellbooks, or gear without uses.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

item.description: The name of the consumable item.

name: recharge_relic
description: Restore a relic to its full uses, once its recharge rule is met. Refused when the relic is already fully charged.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

name: roll_save
description: Roll a save for a character. The engine rolls the die and compares it to the stat, and records the result. A failure does not defeat the character; apply what the save costs yourself.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

reason.description: What the save is for, such as 'a spell's backlash'.

name: give_item
description: Add an item a character is given, found, or looted, with no payment. Petty items (such as scrolls) take no slot; normal items take one; bulky items take two. A full inventory (10 slots) reduces the character to 0 HP. Never use it for something the character pays for, including from a shopkeeper who lets them pay later: use buy_item, which takes the gold and refuses if it cannot. There is no credit.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

size.description: The item's size: 'petty' takes no slot, 'normal' takes one, 'bulky' takes two. Defaults to 'normal'.

name: search_marketplace
description: Find goods and services for sale by words in their name, category, or description. Every word in the query must appear. Each item gives its price, size, and description, and each service gives its price. Use these prices when a character buys with buy_item or buy_service.

query.description: Words to look for, such as 'rope' or 'armor'.

name: buy_item
description: Use this for every sale: the character pays gold and the item goes into their inventory. A catalogue item (see search_marketplace) costs its listed price, so leave price out. For anything else, give a price you set from similar catalogue items. Armor adds to the buyer's armor. There is no credit: a purchase is refused if the character lacks the gold or the room, and a shopkeeper cannot give a thing on a promise to pay later.

name.description: The name of the buying character.

item.description: The name of the item, as listed in the catalogue when it is there.

price.description: Gold to pay. Only for items not in the catalogue; a catalogue item's price must match its listing if given.

size.description: The size of an item not in the catalogue. Catalogue items keep their listed size.

name: buy_service
description: The named characters buy a service, such as a room for the night or medical healing. The first character named pays for the whole service. Lodging covers the party a night, and a lodged character needs no food on the next rest. Healing restores all harm, HP and attributes, for each named character who has lost any.

names.description: The characters the service is for. The first one pays.

service.description: The service's id or name, as listed by search_marketplace.

name: drop_item
description: Remove an item from a character's inventory. Use it when the character drops something, or must drop an item to make room for Fatigue. Gold is not an item and cannot be dropped. Never use it to eat, drink, or spend food or another consumable: use use_item for that, and rest eats rations itself. Dropping a stack removes all of its uses.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

item.description: The name of the item to drop.
